text: In 1776, two American founding fathers, John Adams and Benjamin Franklin, had to share a tiny bed at a crowded inn. Adams closed the window because he was afraid of the cold night air. Franklin opened it again, and lectured him about his theory of colds… until Adams fell asleep.

text: Sleep comes in cycles of about ninety minutes. And in 1953, two scientists in Chicago noticed something weird: every so often, sleeping people's eyes start moving fast under their eyelids. They called it R-E-M, rapid eye movement. Wake someone up during it, and they'll usually tell you a dream.

text: The oldest earplugs in any story are made of beeswax. In Homer's Odyssey, Odysseus plugs his sailors' ears so they won't hear the deadly song of the Sirens. Then in 1907, a German pharmacist named Max Negwer read that story and started selling wax earplugs. His company still makes them today.
